title: Why your bank pays you 1% and charges you 20%
description:
The gap between what a bank pays savers and charges borrowers is not a fee. It is the business.

New video every day.

scenes.say: Your bank pays you about one percent on your savings. The same bank charges you about twenty percent on your card.
That gap is not a fee you can avoid. It is the entire business.
A bank is not a safe place that keeps your money. It is a shop that buys money cheaply and sells it expensively.
It buys from savers at one percent. It sells to borrowers at twenty. The nineteen in between is what pays for everything.
Which tells you which side of that counter you want to stand on, and how expensive it is to stand on the wrong one.
You are not a customer of a bank. You are either its supplier or its product.
